Title: An analytics-based assessment of sales channel portfolios and revenue performance under disruption and recovery
Authors: Salmani Y.; Zhong Y.; Li Y.; Ariannejad A.; Mousavian S.
Abstract: This study develops an analytics-based framework to evaluate how sales channel portfolios influence firm revenue performance under disruption and recovery. Using quarterly data from 84 U.S. manufacturing firms from Q4 2019 to 2023, we apply association rule mining to identify recurrent patterns linking channel configurations, product characteristics, and cross-channel fulfillment mechanisms to revenue outcomes. This approach enables the detection of complex, time-varying relationships difficult to capture using conventional econometric models. Retailer-based portfolios are consistently associated with stronger revenue performance across both phases, while online channel effectiveness varies by product type and portfolio structure. Physical store and outlet channels are more frequently linked to weaker outcomes. During recovery, online channels exhibit more stable positive associations, and outlet channels are associated with improved performance primarily for search products. Buy-online-pickup-in-store and curbside fulfillment mechanisms display limited and inconsistent revenue effects. The findings indicate a structural shift in channel portfolio strategies, from concentrated and hybrid configurations under disruption toward broader multichannel portfolios during recovery, consistent with a pattern of simplification followed by reconfiguration. By demonstrating how association rule mining can uncover channel-performance patterns, this study contributes to marketing analytics research and provides decision-support insights for managers seeking to design resilient, data-driven omnichannel strategies. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.

Title: The “Green Spotlight” Effect: How Facial Recognition Promotes Public Sustainable Consumption
Authors: Zhang Y.; Qu M.; Chen N.; Zhu L.
Abstract: With the rise of artificial intelligence, facial recognition technology has increasingly become an essential part of our daily lives, gradually replacing traditional methods of identity verification. While prior research has focused on consumer acceptance of facial recognition technology as a consequential variable, limited literature has paid attention to its downstream effects on consumer behavior. This paper aims to fill this research gap by investigating the role of facial recognition technology as an antecedent in consumer decision-making. Through five studies, the findings demonstrate that exposure to facial recognition (vs. non-facial recognition) technology leads consumers to exhibit a stronger preference for sustainable products over conventional alternatives. Furthermore, impression management mediates the effect of facial recognition technology on sustainable consumption. In addition, the purchase context (public vs. private) moderates this effect. Facial recognition technology (compared to non-facial recognition) increases consumers' intention to choose sustainable products in public consumption, but not in private ones. This research connects facial recognition technology with sustainable consumption, offering novel theoretical and practical directions for marketing decisions. © 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.
Keywords: facial recognition; impression management; private consumption; public consumption; sustainable consumer behavior

Because the effect is mediated by impression management and depends on public vs. private context, the purpose aligns with understanding customer responses/psychological mechanisms (feeling AI) in marketing research.

Title: Deconstruction and Interpretation of Advertising Cost-Conversion Efficiency: Microlevel Feature Analysis Based on Machine Learning and SHAP
Authors: Huang J.; Liu R.; Zhou Y.
Abstract: Precisely deconstructing the numerical composition of advertising cost-conversion efficiency (ACTE) and uncovering its microlevel associative mechanisms are critical for enterprises to optimize marketing decisions. To overcome the limitations of existing methods regarding modeling accuracy and result interpretability, this study constructs an analytical framework integrating machine learning with interpretable artificial intelligence. Using 174,584 real-world microlevel advertising records from a Chinese telecommunications company in July 2024, we systematically compared six representative machine learning models, rigorously evaluating them against a historical average baseline. The findings reveal that the XGBoost model achieves optimal fitting and generalization performance, with a test set coefficient of determination of 0.8236 ± 0.2061, significantly outperforming the baseline and other models. Furthermore, SHAP-based interpretability analysis not only precisely quantifies the contribution of each feature to the ACTE value but also systematically reveals underlying nonlinear dependencies and threshold effects. Specifically, the advertising conversion rate plays a dominant role; exposure frequency shows a step-like positive association; production cost exhibits a reversal effect demarcated by the median; click-through rate and play volume display discrete stratified structures; and average display cost contributes minimally. Specification tests indicate that ACTE interpretability primarily stems from algebraic relationships of constitutive features, with limited independent contributions from non-constitutive features. Theoretically, this study provides microlevel evidence for nonlinear advertising associations; methodologically, it establishes a rigorous modeling-to-interpretation paradigm; and practically, it offers empirically grounded decision support for advertising exposure regulation and cost optimization. © 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

Title: AI-generated tourism visuals for generation alpha travelers: A contingency theory framework for destination marketing technology integration
Authors: Hassan T.; Saleh M.I.
Abstract: Despite the growing influence of Generation Alpha as tourism decision-makers, limited research examines their distinct destination preferences and responses to AI-generated marketing content. This study examines Generation Alpha's tourism destination preferences using AI-generated visual scenarios and Contingency Theory. The study employs a mixed-methods sequential design: interviews with Generation Alpha participants to identify preferred destination attributes using DALL-E and MidJourney; surveys of 378 Generation Alpha participants; and ANOVA tests to examine preference differences and gender variations across AI-generated tourism scenarios. Theoretically, the findings are interpreted through a contingency lens, in which generational cohort characteristics may act as a contextual contingency associated with differing preferences for AI-generated tourism marketing. Practically, findings inform tourism marketers in developing gender-differentiated AI content strategies that emphasize collaborative experiences for females and autonomous exploration for males, while prioritizing technological innovation and extreme-adventure accessibility in destination positioning to maximize engagement with this emerging consumer segment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence in Marketing Education: Preparing Students for an AI-Driven Future
Authors: Riley J.; Harvey E.S.; Hain J.S.; Green P.; VanMeter R.
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming marketing practice, yet marketing education has struggled to keep pace with these technological changes. As AI tools become embedded in marketing analytics, content development, and strategic decision-making, business programs face increasing pressure to prepare graduates with the competencies required for AI-enabled marketing environments. This manuscript develops a systems-level framework for integrating AI into marketing education, building on prior applications of Marketing Systems Theory. The framework conceptualizes marketing education as an adaptive subsystem that responds to technological disruption and positions AI integration as a coordination problem across institutional, faculty, and student levels. Within this framework, AI is treated as a decision-support capability rather than a tool outcome, emphasizing auditing, ethical judgment, and accountability. AI competencies are positioned as a portfolio of capabilities, including prompt engineering, data literacy, ethical awareness, and critical evaluation of AI outputs, rather than isolated technical skills. The paper concludes with implications for curriculum design and a proposed research agenda addressing governance, credentialing, and workforce alignment in AI-driven marketing systems. © 2026 Society for Marketing Advances.

Therefore, the stage and AI purpose within marketing decision-making cannot be identified from the abstract.

Title: When product strategy meets platform reality: field evidence on bundle performance in digital markets
Authors: Chang K.-F.; Sauber M.H.; Hsu M.K.; Huang A.
Abstract: Consider a paradox at the heart of marketing strategy: managers devote substantial effort to determining what products should be bundled and how those bundles should be priced, yet comparatively little attention is paid to whether the message describing the bundle reflects the same value logic through which customers evaluate it. Product bundling has long been recognized as a powerful mechanism for increasing perceived value, reducing consumer search costs, encouraging trial, and enhancing firm profitability (Stremersch & Tellis 2002; Venkatesh & Mahajan 1993). Yet even carefully designed bundles often underperform when the rationale communicated to customers fails to align with the value they seek from the offering. This research proposes “communication bundling” as a theoretical construct distinct from integrated marketing communications and multichannel strategy, and introduces a synchronization matrix that quantifies product-communication alignment as the mechanism linking Quality Function Deployment (product configuration) with Elaboration Likelihood Model principles (platform-specific communication). We derive four testable propositions and evaluate them through a quasi-experimental field study of 31 companies across four industries in China over 6 months. Synchronized strategies improved ROI by 42.3% (95% CI: 38.1%-46.5%, p <.001, d = 1.47) and AI-agent-mediated conversions by 161%, compared to 38.4% among traditional consumers, a pattern consistent with algorithmic systems rewarding product-communication coherence more than human consumers do. Mediation analysis identifies alignment quality as the primary mechanism, accounting for 67% of total effects. The synchronization matrix’s alignment scores correlate strongly with subsequent performance gains (r = 0.72, p <.001), confirming the framework's predictive validity. Three of four propositions receive strong empirical support; one receives partial support. All gains resulted from reallocation of existing marketing spend rather than incremental budget increases. Methodologically, this research contributes a validated diagnostic and optimization tool for marketing analytics: the synchronization matrix generates measurable alignment scores enabling data-driven reallocation decisions. Theoretically, the findings demonstrate that in algorithmically mediated markets, alignment between product configuration and communication strategy, rather than their independent optimization, drives bundle performance. As algorithmic intermediaries expand toward conversational commerce, synchronization transitions from competitive advantage to market-access requirement. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2026.
Keywords: Algorithmic distribution; Communication strategy; Digital marketing strategy; Platform marketing; Product bundling; Synchronization

Title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Transforming Marketing Strategies and Its Impact on Consumer Buying Behaviour and Brand Engagement in the Indian Retail Sector
Authors: Shafi S.I.; Fazili A.I.
Abstract: The present research explores retail consumer behaviour in the Indian marketing context, focusing on AI-based marketing principles such as AI-driven personalisation, chatbot effectiveness, and predictive analytics, and their effects on consumer trust, purchase intention, brand engagement, and customer loyalty. The study adopts a quantitative research approach with a descriptive research design. Data were collected through structured online questionnaires administered to approximately 450 respondents across selected locations in India. The collected data were analysed using descriptive statistics, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), structural equation modeling (SEM), and hierarchical regression to examine the relationships among variables. The findings reveal that AI-driven personalisation has a significant positive impact on purchase intentions, while chatbot efficiency, consumer trust, and predictive analytics positively influence brand engagement. The results further indicate that consumer trust plays a crucial role in shaping purchasing decisions and strengthening brand engagement, ultimately leading to customer loyalty. Overall, the study highlights that AI technologies significantly influence the customer decision-making process by delivering customised advertising and efficient customer service, thereby enhancing long-term brand relationships. © 2026 SCMS Group of Educational Institutions. All rights reserved.

Title: Transformative marketing strategies in the era of new-age technologies: Principles, plan, purpose, and practice
Authors: Kumar V.; Kotler P.; Kumar A.
Abstract: New age technologies (NATs) such as generative AI (GAI), agentic AI, the metaverse, and blockchain, among others, are revolutionizing how firms engage with consumers, deliver value, create new content, and personalize experiences at various levels (e.g., brand, product, product line, business unit, and firm). This study is based on the premise that the influence of NATs on the marketing strategies of firms as well as the marketing strategy formulation process is growing rapidly. Based on this premise, this study explores the following four questions: (1) What are transformative marketing strategies (Principles)? (2) How are they developed (Plan)? (3) Why are they needed (Purpose)? and (4) Where can they be used (Practice)? Accordingly, this study considers seven popular marketing strategies firms use—pricing, distribution, product, promotion, selling, global market entry, and innovation—that are included in TMS. Using various use cases across these marketing strategies, this study discusses how marketing managers can use these NATs to enhance productivity, create personalized marketing experiences, make more informed strategic decisions, and drive higher engagement with minimal manual effort. This study also advances a 2 × 2 matrix—the relative speed of NAT adoption vs. the relative speed of relevant marketing strategy adaptation—that offers a structured framework to help firms integrate and manage these seven strategies for better performance. Through the intersection of NATs and marketing adaptability, this study outlines implications for both research and practice, offers valuable strategies for organizations, proposes several research questions, and establishes a foundation for the future of TMS in the era of NATs. © Academy of Marketing Science 2025.

Title: Bridging Perceived and Projected Destination Images: A Machine Learning-Driven Systemic Network Analysis
Authors: Lin R.; Zhu B.-W.; Xiong L.; Wang G.-Q.; Tzeng G.-H.
Abstract: Understanding the differences between the projected and perceived images of destinations plays a critical role in destination marketing and the fulfillment of tourists' expectations. However, existing research still lacks a systematic explanation of the network-level differences in destination image, and tends to overlook the underlying influence mechanisms among its factors. Using Macau as a case study, this research develops a decision-making model to deepen the understanding of interrelationships among destination image factors, and to explore the structural network differences between images. To achieve this, the research employs Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), quadrant analysis, and the Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) method. This study offers a systematic perspective to narrow the gap between the projected and perceived image. The results enable DMOs to gain deeper insights into tourists’ needs and perceptions, as well as to identify the key factors shaping destination image, and the internal influence relationships among its components. © The Author(s) 2026

Title: Informing or persuading? How AI chatbot language styles shape tourists’ visit intentions
Authors: Huang L.; Wang C.; Guo J.
Abstract: The increasing use of artificial intelligence chatbots in tourism is reshaping how tourists process information and make destination decisions. This study adopts a communicative-goal perspective to conceptualize chatbot language style as either informative or persuasive and examines their differential effects on tourists’ visit intention. Drawing on language expectancy theory and evidence from three experimental studies, the findings show that persuasive language is more effective than informative language in enhancing visit intentions. Further analyses reveal that emotional arousal serves as a key mediating mechanism in the relationship between language style and visit intention. In addition, the findings identify important boundary conditions: tourists with lower levels of AI literacy are more responsive to persuasive language, whereas those with higher perceived risk exhibit a stronger preference for informative language. By extending language expectancy theory to AI-driven communication contexts, this study deepens understanding of chatbot–tourist interactions and highlights language style as a critical design element in AI-assisted destination marketing. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Influencer selection under budget constraints: a learning approach
Authors: Xu Z.; Xing X.; Tiwari S.
Abstract: Influencer marketing is becoming the fastest-growing and most cost-effective form of marketing and advertising. In this paper, we consider an influencer selection problem in online learning and adaptive settings: a brand conducts influencer marketing campaigns to promote a product over multiple rounds with a limited promotional budget. We propose a cumulative oversampling (CO) technique for Thompson Sampling (TS) that can be used to construct optimistic parameter estimates using significantly fewer samples from the posterior distributions compared to existing oversampling frameworks. By combining CO with the oracle we designed for the offline problem, our online learning algorithm simultaneously addresses budget allocation, parameter learning, and reward maximisation. We prove that our online learning algorithm achieves a scaled regret comparable to that of the UCB-based algorithms for the Influence Maximisation problem. It is the first regret bound for TS-based algorithms for IM semi-bandits that does not depend linearly on the reciprocal of the minimum observation probability of an edge. Our results provide actionable insights for firms on how to allocate marketing budgets and select influencers in dynamic and uncertain environments. © 2026 The Operational Research Society.
Keywords: budgeted influence maximisation; Influencer marketing; prediction and adaptive decision making; regret analysis; Thompson sampling
Journal: Journal of the Operational Research Society
evidence: We propose a cumulative oversampling (CO) technique for Thompson Sampling (TS) that can be used to construct optimistic parameter estimates.
rationale: The purpose is adaptive decision-making for influencer selection under budget constraints across campaign rounds, optimizing reward/promotion outcomes. This is a marketing action decision about promotional resource allocation (promotion/communication) using thinking AI.

Title: How to select the optimal bundling strategy for two products within a sales cycle
Authors: Zhang Y.; Meng Z.
Abstract: Purpose – The most difficult problem in bundled sales is how to choose the two most suitable bundled products among a large number of sold products in the retail or online sales market. This article develops an optimal bundling strategy model for two products with demand uncertainty within a single sales cycle. Design/methodology/approach – By introducing bundling purchasing intentions for the sale of two products together, a profit-maximizing model for bundled sales is established. It has been proven that there is always an optimal bundling quantity of two products in the retail market through our model. An algorithm is then designed to determine the optimal bundling strategy. Findings – The numerical analysis results indicate that the algorithm for the optimal bundling strategy can yield the planned bundling quantities for the two products corresponding to the maximum expected profit, as well as the expected profit itself. This research addresses the theoretical problem of selecting the optimal bundling strategy for two products within a sales cycle, which holds significant guiding value for the study and practice of bundling sales strategies and a bundling strategy model for ordering bundled products for inventory management. Research limitations/implications – (1) Participating Data Mining Techniques: Investigate how to obtain the appropriate value of bundling purchasing intentions under different large models or algorithms using data mining techniques. (2) Analyzing with different Probability Distributions: Examine the impact of different probability distributions on bundling strategies and optimal order quantities. (3) Introducing the influence of Online Advertisement: Explore the influence of different types of online advertising on bundling outcomes. (4) Constructing discount Bundling Pricing Models: Construct discount bundling pricing models to enhance research on bundling strategies when implementing discounted sales for bundled products. Practical implications – This article proposes a strategy selection methodology for optimal planned bundling quantity, whereas existing theoretical research on product bundling has primarily concentrated on the domain of economy and psychology. And in implementing intelligent decision-making, it has been proven that there always exists an optimal bundling strategy. The introduction of bundling purchasing intentions reduces the difficulty of solving the two product bundling models. Social implications – E-retail industry has rich and sufficient historical sales data for implementing intelligent decision-making. Merchants widely adopt product bundling strategies to increase sales and profits. Based on the periodic newsboy model, this study introduces the bundling purchasing intentions, constructs the optimal bundling strategy model for the associated products, and investigates the expressions for their optimal bundling strategies and expected profits. These theoretical researches contribute practical value for explaining the bundling strategy of e-commerce. Originality/value – The optimal bundling model of two products for sales is proposed. The bundling purchasing intentions reduce the difficulty of solving the bundling model. Prove that there always exists an optimal bundling strategy for two products. An algorithm is designed to determine the optimal bundling strategy. Determine whether two products are suitable for bundling based on the bundling purchasing intentions. © Emerald Publishing Limited

Title: A framework for authentic marketing in the age of artificial intelligence
Authors: Winter S.
Abstract: The acceleration of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped the marketing landscape. Today, optimised content can be created with a single prompt, advertising campaigns can be automated from start to finish, and websites can be designed in minutes. But how much of a discipline built on human emotion, decision-making and behavioural insight should be handed over to machines? Where do we draw the line? This paper explores one of the most pressing challenges for modern marketers: maintaining authenticity in an era dominated by algorithmic feeds and automation. It highlights the balancing act of keeping pace with rapidly evolving technologies while retaining the foundational elements of effective marketing that require slower, more strategic thought. Drawing on global research and industry insights, the paper presents a practical five-part framework to help marketing leaders integrate AI in ways that increase trust, strengthen brand narratives and improve long-term audience relationships. Throughout, the paper provides examples of how AI can be deployed to enable, not erode, authenticity in marketing practice. © HENRY STEWART PUBLICATIONS 2050-0084 (2026).
Journal: Journal of Digital and Social Media Marketing
evidence: This paper explores one of the most pressing challenges for modern marketers: maintaining authenticity in an era dominated by algorithmic feeds and automation.

Title: Clustering sustainable tourism destinations through Instagram photo analysis: a machine learning approach
Authors: Basirati M.; Laachach A.
Abstract: Purpose – This study uses advanced machine learning (ML) techniques to analyze Instagram photos and cluster sustainable tourism destinations. By revealing visual patterns and themes, it provides valuable insights into user-generated content (UGC) and its influence on destination image formation. Using established methods such as k-means clustering and semantic analysis, this study aims to enhance sustainable tourism promotion by optimizing targeted marketing strategies and improving the overall tourist experience. Design/methodology/approach – This study uses ML to analyze Instagram images through a four-step approach. The authors collected 208 posts and 1, 890 images, ensuring data accuracy via cleansing. Each image was labeled for machine understanding using the Doc2Vec model to capture semantic meaning from captions. Finally, the authors applied k-means clustering to group posts based on similarities in visual motifs and hashtag usage, enhancing interpretability and contributing to the field of image classification through advanced ML techniques. Findings – This study demonstrates that ML effectively clusters sustainable tourism destinations on Instagram, identifying four key themes: “Natural landscapes, ” “Historical and archaeological, ” “Branding and graphics” and “Cultural heritage.” Popular destinations like Marrakech, Aït Bouguemez and Dakhla dominate image concentrations. These insights provide actionable strategies for promoting sustainability, enhancing destination branding and tailoring marketing approaches for Morocco and similar global destinations. Practical implications – The research contributes to the global effort to address how Morocco’s commitment to sustainable tourism can be included in the Sustainable Development Goals. It provides insights into forecasting regional tourism demand and coastal management strategies for sustainable tourism development in Morocco. Originality/value – This paper offers data-driven insights into the visual representation of sustainable tourism destinations, thereby providing a valuable resource for policymakers and practitioners seeking to inform their decisions and actions. The proposed method can be leveraged to inform policy and practice in sustainable tourism, ultimately supporting local businesses and promoting eco-friendly travel practices. © 2025 Emerald Publishing Limited

Title: AI-enabled consumer digital twins as a platform for research aimed at enhancing customer experience
Authors: Hornik J.; Rachamim M.
Abstract: Consumer behavior is monitored and analyzed by innumerable obtrusive and non-obtrusive autonomous devices, technologies, surveys, models, and software. In recent years, with the advent of digitization, the research of consumer behavior has undergone a major transformation, yielding complex, extensive, and diverse consumer data. This data diversity is liable to hinder consumer research. Therefore, there is a clear need to integrate and synthesize the large-scale data centers conforming to predefined decision rules and research objectives. Against this backdrop, this contribution proposes to the marketing and consumer research community a new platform for data fusion and consumer modeling—consumer digital twins (CDTs). Although numerous research studies have been published on human digital twins (HDTs), none have been conducted in the management and consumer domains. The study aims to bridge two perspectives: on the one hand, the authors acknowledge the value of CDT as a consumer data fusion platform, while on the other hand, they build on previous scholarship to propose a conceptual framework for implementing the platform in future research, using as an example a CDT designed for customer journey optimization. © The Author(s) 2025.

Title: Decoding community enterprise sales performance drivers: visual analytics with heatmaps and decision trees
Authors: Klubsakul O.-P.; Oan-Oon R.
Abstract: Community enterprises in Thailand’s secondary provinces struggle to identify which marketing factors drive sales performance. This study fills that gap by applying visual analytics and explainable machine learning to community enterprise operators in Chai Nat province. Using a sequential mixed-methods design, we combined semi-structured interviews with 21 key informants and a structured survey of 383 enterprise operators. The quantitative analytical stage—consisting of Pearson correlation, stepwise multiple regression, correlation heatmaps, and Gini-based decision trees—identified the hierarchical drivers of sales variance. Distribution channel effectiveness and value-based pricing emerged as the two dominant predictors, jointly explaining 31.5% of the variance. Product quality and promotion functioned as standardized baseline prerequisites rather than competitive differentiators. Decision tree analysis identified the point of transaction, product visibility, frictionless digital ordering, and secure payment as the critical catalysts for sales performance. For practitioners and policymakers, sustainable growth requires investing in customer-centric digital logistics and transactional convenience. Methodologically, this study shows how visual analytics and interpretable machine learning enhance transparency in applied business analytics, offering a replicable framework for similar resource-constrained regional markets. © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Does paying for visibility pay off? The impact of sponsored recommendations on UGC platforms
Authors: Zhao W.; Feng H.; Feng N.; Li M.
Abstract: AbstractUser-generated content (UGC) platforms are characterized by creators producing content and competing for audience attention. As these platforms mature, monetization tools such as sponsored recommendations—which allow creators to pay for enhanced visibility—have become increasingly prominent. However, their implications for platform profitability and creator competition remain unclear, especially in settings where platforms share advertising revenue with creators and where creators can also attract audiences through off-platform promotion. In this paper, we examine UGC platforms' decisions on whether to introduce sponsored recommendations and how to allocate traffic optimally between paid and organic visibility. Using a game-theoretic model, we show that sponsored recommendations are optimal when creators retain a large share of advertising revenue and face high content creation costs. In contrast, when creators receive a smaller revenue share or incur lower marginal effort costs, avoiding sponsored recommendations maximizes platform revenue. We further find that creators invest in platform-based promotion only when paid visibility exceeds a critical threshold, while they consistently pursue off-platform audience acquisition regardless of platform policy. Importantly, although sponsored recommendations can boost short-term platform revenue, excessive reliance on paid promotion reduces content creation effort, weakens off-platform marketing, and limits long-term audience growth. As a result, returns decline for both the platform and creators. Finally, in settings with heterogeneous creators, higher levels of paid visibility further amplify the advantage of high-effectiveness creators in attracting and retaining audiences. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: Strategic framework for digital marketing localization: advancing the standardization-adaptation debate in international marketing strategy
Authors: Elhajjar S.; El Nemar S.; Theofanous G.; Mouline J.-P.
Abstract: Purpose – This conceptual paper responds to the evolving needs of international marketing strategy (IMS) by proposing a theoretically grounded Digital Marketing Localization Framework (DMLF). The framework revisits the standardization versus adaptation debate, emphasizing its relevance in digitally mediated environments. Design/methodology/approach – A structured literature review was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar (1983–mid-2025) pertaining to IMS frameworks, digital platforms, cross-cultural behavior and decision-making models. Several peer-reviewed articles and book chapters were included, while studies limited to traditional media or the B2B context were excluded. This synthesis incorporates key classical debates regarding IMS, and advances in digital ecosystems, personalization and cultural engagement. Drawing on an interdisciplinary approach that blends theoretical constructs from interrelated fields, this paper develops a structured, multi-dimensional decision-making framework. Findings – The study highlights the importance of integrating cultural sensitivity, platform-specific dynamics and algorithmic personalization into IMS theory. It addresses gaps in pre-digital frameworks by offering actionable insights for navigating the complexities introduced by digital platforms and cross-border data governance. Research limitations/implications – As a conceptual study, the framework requires empirical validation through future research. Our paper outlines testable propositions and methodologies to evaluate the effectiveness of DMLF across diverse markets. Future researchers need to focus on examining the unresolved tensions between; AI-driven efficiency and culturally embedded authenticity, automation compared to cultural sensitivity, standardization logic compared to adaptive learning, algorithmic optimization compared to managerial judgment and their impact on local decision-making. Practical implications – The DMLF provides actionable guidance for marketing executives to balance global coherence with local relevance. It enables organizations to systematically evaluate digital localization options, ensuring decisions are guided by contextual insights rather than intuition. Originality/value – This research contributes to IMS by adapting foundational debates to the complexities of digital globalization. It offers a comprehensive framework tailored to internet-enabled international operations and proposes an agenda for empirical research that aligns with IMS's broader shift toward analytical rigor and theoretical innovation. © Emerald Publishing Limited

Title: Transforming Banking Culture in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: The Role of AI Trust, Algorithmic Transparency and Financial Confidence in Customer Loyalty
Authors: Yamarthi S.; Balaji Ch.; Mobasheer S.; Khan M.A.; Kannaiah P.
Abstract: The rapid integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the banking sector is transforming not only financial service delivery but also the cultural foundations of customer–bank relationships. AI-driven banking has introduced new forms of interaction, decision-making, personalization, and service automation, making customer trust in intelligent technologies increasingly important. This study examines how AI trust, algorithmic transparency, and financial confidence contribute to customer loyalty in the changing culture of AI-enabled banking. The study conceptualizes banking culture as an evolving environment shaped by technological adoption, perceptions of fairness, transparency, security, and confidence in automated financial decision-making. AI trust reflects customers’ perceptions of the reliability, competence, security, and ethical use of AI systems, while algorithmic transparency concerns the extent to which customers perceive AI-driven decisions and recommendations as understandable and explainable. Financial confidence represents customers’ perceived ability and assurance to engage with AI-enabled financial services and make informed financial decisions. Drawing upon trust, technology adoption, relationship marketing, and consumer behaviour perspectives, the study proposes that AI trust and algorithmic transparency enhance financial confidence, which subsequently strengthens customer satisfaction, engagement, and loyalty. The study further argues that transparent and trustworthy AI can reduce perceived technological and financial risks, strengthen customer–bank relationships, and reduce switching intentions. The findings are expected to contribute to the emerging literature on the transformation of banking culture by demonstrating how technological trust and transparency shape contemporary customer behaviour and long-term loyalty. The study also provides practical implications for banks seeking to develop responsible, transparent, culturally responsive, and customer-centric AI ecosystems. © 2026 Slovenian Sociological Association. Title: Evaluating Novel Unstructured Treatments with Generative AI: A Causal Prediction Framework
Authors: Ellickson P.B.; Kar W.; Reeder J.C., III; Zeng G.
Abstract: Modern marketing increasingly requires managers to deploy new content at scale, often with limited opportunity for prior testing. As a result, decisions about what to launch become strategic managerial choices under uncertainty rather than purely creative exercises. While generative AI (GenAI) makes the creation of new content fast and highly scalable, it simultaneously expands the set of options managers must evaluate, making reliable content selection increasingly difficult. The authors develop a framework for causal prediction that enables managers to evaluate and deploy novel marketing content generated by AI. The framework uses pretrained large language models to represent previously deployed content and learn how its features causally relate to outcomes. Using a rejection-sampling procedure, the framework screens new content proposed by GenAI to avoid extrapolation beyond what historical data can reliably support. In a large-scale email marketing application (3.3 million observations across 34 campaigns), the framework improves out-of-sample prediction and real-world deployment performance relative to standard approaches, enabling outcome-guided generation of higher-performing AI-generated content. The framework establishes a threshold based on how closely new content resembles past campaigns, separating cases where causal prediction is reliable from cases where direct experimentation is warranted. The framework has important implications for marketing decision-making in a rapidly evolving environment where GenAI is transforming content creation and deployment. © 2026. Title: When and how AI personalization drives sustainable purchases: The roles of relevance, privacy, and transparency in eco-friendly advertising
Authors: Qadri U.A.; Ahmed Moustafa A.M.; Waqas M.
Abstract: AI-driven personalization uses algorithmic tailoring to deliver content aligned with consumers’ preferences. Although prior research suggests that personalized sustainability messages can influence green behavior by enhancing perceived message relevance, the literature has not systematically examined how this relevance pathway is disrupted by privacy concerns or repaired by AI transparency disclosures. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model, Self-Congruity Theory, and Privacy Calculus Theory, this research conceptualizes perceived message relevance as the key mechanism through which AI-driven personalization promotes sustainable purchase intention. Across two studies, a scenario-based experiment and a time-lagged field survey in China, this research demonstrates that the effect of AI personalization on sustainable purchase intention is mediated by perceived relevance and conditionally moderated by privacy concern and AI transparency. Specifically, privacy concern weakens, and AI transparency strengthens, the personalization–relevance pathway. The findings are robust across experimental and real-world e-commerce contexts and clarify when AI personalization is likely to succeed or fail in motivating sustainable behavior. In particular, relevance emerges as a persuasion route that depends on the presence of ethical and transparent personalization cues. Managerial implications for designing privacy-respectful, transparency-rich personalization strategies in green advertising are presented. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Artificial intelligence in halal product marketing: integrating ethical intelligence through a mixed-method investigation
Authors: Rahman W.
Abstract: Purpose – This study tackles the ethical integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in halal marketing. It tests how AI transparency, authenticity and value alignment shape Muslim consumer trust and buying decisions. The purpose of this study is to bridge rapid technological change with the foundational moral duties required by Islamic commerce. Design/methodology/approach – The author used a two-phase explanatory sequential design. In the first phase, the author surveyed 980 Muslim consumers across Bangladesh, Malaysia and the United Arab Emirates and analysed the data using partial least squares structural equation modelling with multi-group and mediation checks. In the second phase, the author conducted 24 interviews with halal industry professionals to interpret the statistical results in a real-world context. Findings – AI transparency, authenticity and value alignment drive consumer trust, which partially mediates their impact on purchase intention. The model held steady across all three nations. Interviews highlighted genuine practitioner fears about algorithmic bias, exposed the urgent need for Shariah-compliant data and confirmed that moral accountability is non-negotiable in AI-driven halal marketing. Research limitations/implications – The cross-sectional design and focus on three Muslim-majority countries limit causality and global generalisability. Theoretically, the author reframes AI transparency as a moral obligation and combines Islamic philosophy with marketing science. The author also introduces “theological-affective legitimacy” as a new touchstone for trust in digital faith-based environments. Practical implications – Marketers must prioritise explainable AI and craft communications that feel culturally sincere. Developers need “Shariah-by-design” principles and diverse training data to cut through bias. Policymakers should embed ethics rules directly into halal certification processes to make compliance tangible and enforceable. Social implications – This work arms Muslim consumers with ethical AI literacy, enabling them to demand openness and make spiritually conscious purchases. It encourages a digital marketplace that respects religious identity and actively guards against algorithmic colonialism, where outside data norms overwhelm local moral frameworks. Originality/value – This study offers the first empirical test, to the best of the author’s knowledge, of the ethical intelligence framework, showing transparency as the most powerful trust-builder and confirming the model works across diverse markets. This moves the conversation from abstract theory to a practical, integrated model that connects AI functionality with Islamic ethics and consumer psychology for faith-sensitive adoption. © 2026 Emerald Publishing Limited

Title: Kalakrit's dilemma: scaling up business through human expertise or AI
Authors: Dam L.B.; Chaudhary S.
Abstract: Learning outcomes – By analyzing and discussing the case, students should be able to: Examine the role of innovation in entrepreneurial progression. Assess business expansion approaches through diversification. Develop strategic decision-making skills. Analyze the trade-offs between human expertise and AI for achieving the scalability of business. Case overview/synopsis – The case explores Kalakrit's journey as a translation and localization startup. It highlights the challenges faced by its founder, Sehaj, including client acquisition, cost efficiency and competition from AI-driven translation tools. The case examines how Kalakrit leveraged human expertise, innovative cost-cutting and grassroots marketing to scale its business. The discussion links Kalakrit's model to the scalability of business model theory. It shows how the company built a distributed workforce of linguists and voice-over artists, focusing on Kalakrit's unconventional strategies, such as home-based voice-over studios and decentralized audiobook production. Parallels are also drawn to business expansion through diversification. Students will assess the sustainability of these strategies. They will analyze the long-term value of human-driven localization in an AI-driven industry. The case encourages discussion on startup scaling business models in the face of disruptive innovation. It also raises a key question: Should Kalakrit adopt AI-driven translation to achieve the scalability of business operations or position itself as a premium human-led service provider? Title: From emotional data to decisions: A systematic review on how airlines use sentiments and emotions to stay ahead
Authors: Antunes F.; Freire M.; Melo P.; Costa J.P.
Abstract: This study examines the application of sentiment analysis (SA) and emotion detection (ED) within the airline industry. Using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology, we identified and evaluated relevant literature from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (2014–2024), yielding 60 high-quality studies. The results are organized into four thematic clusters: customer analysis, crisis management, business improvements, and analytics techniques. In customer analysis, SA/ED techniques are used to process feedback from social media, review sites, and surveys, enhancing service quality and brand reputation. The crisis management section demonstrates how these methods facilitate the early detection of issues and prompt timely responses during disruptions. Business improvements are addressed through demand forecasting, marketing optimization, and operational adjustment. The analytics techniques section evidences a shift in SA from traditional lexicon-based methods to advanced machine learning, deep learning, and hybrid approaches, including transformer-based models. We also highlight research gaps, emphasizing the need for robust real-time systems and improved multilingual data handling. Overall, the findings underscore the potential of SA/ED to drive agile, customer-centric strategies and invite further exploration into integrated analytical models for the airline industry. © 2025 The Authors

Title: From the Boardroom to the Classroom: What the Emerging Chief Marketing Officer Agenda Reveals About Future Marketer Readiness
Authors: Pettiette M.; Fischbach S.; Whitler K.A.
Abstract: Marketing education has long emphasized work and career readiness, but the meaning of readiness is changing as marketing work is reshaped by artificial intelligence, accountability pressures, shifting role boundaries, and machine-mediated branding and discovery. Although prior research has advanced conversations about employability, career readiness, experiential learning, and artificial intelligence (AI) integration, less attention has been given to how senior marketing leaders’ perceptions of these changes should inform readiness in marketing education. Addressing this gap, this article draws on 15 qualitative interviews with chief marketing officers (CMOs) and senior marketing leaders, reinterpreting a broader thematic analysis through an education-facing lens. The study identifies four broad domains of future marketer readiness: AI-enabled marketing work readiness, strategic judgment and evidence-based decision readiness, marketing accountability readiness, and organizational and role navigation readiness. Two emerging issues are treated as forward-looking manifestations within these domains: hybrid human-AI team management, and AI-mediated discovery, encompassing generative engine optimization (GEO) and brand power in AI-mediated environments. This article’s contribution is translational rather than prescriptive: it treats executive insights as a profession-level signal for understanding marketing work today and how it may evolve, extending the workplace- and career-readiness literature and offering a conceptual framework to guide future research and curriculum reflection. © The Author(s) 2026
